note: The host/device transport, frozen. A request/response mailbox with a monotonic sequence number, chosen because it is the shape a hardware doorbell has: the host writes a descriptor and rings; the device reads it, acts, and writes a completion. Nothing here needs a filesystem to be a filesystem -- swapping the two text files for two MMIO registers changes the medium and not the protocol.
why_not_restart_per_launch: R2-08 RT-02 requires 32 launches in one session with no restart, and R2-11 makes restarting an explicit, observable device-loss recovery rather than a normal path. A one-shot `vvp` per launch would make every launch a recovery, and would make 'the intermediate result stayed in device memory' impossible to claim.

files.req.txt: host -> device. One line: seq op a0 a1 a2 a3 a4 a5. Rewritten in full for each request; the device acts when `seq` exceeds the last one it served.
files.rsp.txt: device -> host. One line: seq status r0 r1. The host polls until `seq` matches its request.
files.up.hex: payload for UPLOAD, one 64-bit word per line, hex

1.name: UPLOAD
1.note: reads up.hex into device memory through the memory system

2.name: DOWNLOAD
2.note: writes down.hex from device memory, through the memory system so a dirty line is seen

3.name: LAUNCH
3.a2: role mask: bit r starts Role Context r; bit 31 (R39-05, RSLICE) gives each started context its own slice of the accumulators, barriers, descriptors and windows, bits 30:29 the log2 of the number of slices (0: one per context the core has); a device without RSLICE ignores them
3.note: All SIX grid values. ISA sec 5.1 makes program_id(axis) the logical index on that axis and num_programs(axis) its extent; carrying only x meant a 2x3 grid handed every program the LINEAR id under the name of the x index, and a kernel cannot tell the difference. Sixteen bits per axis is ample against the 4096-program cap.

4.name: QUIESCE
4.note: returns when the device has no outstanding work: no core busy, no transfer in flight, no memory response owed

5.name: SHUTDOWN
5.note: the only clean way the device stops

6.name: PING
6.note: liveness, and the handshake that proves the device came up

status.1: FAULT -- the kernel trapped; r0 is the trap code, r1 the PC
status.2: TIMEOUT -- the device deadline expired with work outstanding
status.3: REFUSED -- the request was malformed or out of range

rules.sequence: strictly increasing, and a response carries the sequence it answers. A response for an older sequence is a late message from a previous epoch and is discarded by the host, which is what ERR-05 is about.
rules.epoch: recover() starts a new epoch by restarting the device process and incrementing the epoch number. Every handle from a previous epoch is invalid, and a response carrying a previous epoch is discarded rather than believed.
rules.no_hierarchical_access: UPLOAD and DOWNLOAD move data through the device's memory system. Reading a cache tag, a cache data array or a register file by hierarchical reference is forbidden for the product path (MEM-05); the testbench may still do so for its own assertions.
